meta.title: CFD Analysis | novels
meta.description: NOVVES CFD analysis — ventilation and smoke control solutions validated with computational fluid dynamics.

hero.subtitle: Ventilation and smoke control solutions validated with Computational Fluid Dynamics.

intro: As NOVVES, we do not only produce fans, jet fans, smoke extraction fans or ventilation equipment; We develop engineering-based system solutions specific to each project. One of the most important steps of this approach is to numerically validate the design with CFD analysis before implementation into the field.

CFD, i.e. Computational Fluid Dynamics analysis; It enables three-dimensional examination of air flow, smoke dispersion, temperature change, CO concentration and fan effect in indoor parking lots, industrial facilities, technical volumes, tunnel-like structures and large closed areas.

NOVVES evaluates jet fan placement, exhaust fan capacity, fresh air organization, smoke evacuation scenarios and system performance on a project-specific basis with CFD analyses. Thus, engineering-based decisions are made for the correct number of fans, correct fan location, optimum energy use and safer evacuation conditions.

whyCfd.title: Why CFD Analysis?
whyCfd.intro: CFD analysis enables ventilation and smoke control systems to be evaluated based on actual project conditions, not just theoretical calculations.

items.title: System performance is seen before deployment to the field
items.desc: Performance of fan systems; It is simulated by taking into account the project geometry, column placement, ramp positions, ceiling height, exhaust points and fresh air inlets.

items.title: Fire and smoke scenarios are tested in advance
items.desc: It is analyzed in which direction the smoke will spread, in which areas it will concentrate, how it may affect escape routes and how jet fans will direct the smoke.

items.title: Critical variables are evaluated with engineering data
items.desc: Parameters such as visibility, temperature rise, air velocity, CO density, smoke layer, dead zones and exhaust efficiency are examined numerically.

items.title: Regulation and safe evacuation goals are supported
items.desc: CFD analysis; It contributes to more reliable project decisions in terms of smoke control design, parking garage ventilation, fire safety and evacuation scenarios.

whyCfd.resultText: Correct placement, correct number of fans, optimum energy use and maximum security are targeted.

items.title: Airspeed Distribution
items.subtitle: Velocity Analysis
items.text: The direction, speed and distribution of air flow within a closed space are modeled in three dimensions. It is analyzed whether sufficient air circulation is provided throughout the environment with the effect of jet fans.

items.title: Temperature Change
items.subtitle: temperature distribution
items.text: It is evaluated how the ambient temperature changes at the human level, in the ceiling area and in critical escape routes during the fire scenario. By determining critical temperature zones, risks in terms of emergency safety are revealed.

items.title: Visibility Assessment
items.subtitle: Visibility Analysis
items.text: It is analyzed how long visibility can be maintained on escape routes under dense smoke. The reduction in visibility is evaluated in terms of evacuation safety and fire department response.

items.title: Carbon Monoxide Release
items.subtitle: CO Concentration
items.text: CO accumulation due to vehicle exhaust gas is modeled in areas such as closed parking lots. The change in CO concentration over time and how it is evacuated by the fan system is analyzed.

items.title: Smoke Diffusion
items.subtitle: Smoke Propagation
items.text: The direction and speed of smoke spread after a fire, layer formation and how it is directed with the help of jet fans are simulated. The effectiveness of the exhaust points and the performance of the smoke control strategy are evaluated.

items.title: Jet Fan Effect
items.subtitle: Jet Fan Impact
items.text: The effect of jet fans on air flow, their ability to reduce dead zones, their directing performance to exhaust fans and their contribution to air movement within the system are analyzed.

items.title: Exhaust and Fresh Air Balance
items.subtitle: Air Balance
items.text: Exhaust fans, fresh air inlets, natural openings and mechanical supply systems are evaluated together. System balance, pressure differences and air renewal performance are examined.

meta.description: NOVVES smoke control system design — jet fan, smoke evacuation and engineering-oriented solutions for indoor car parks and large volume structures.

hero.subtitle: Engineering-oriented smoke control solutions for indoor parking lots and large-volume structures.

intro: NOVVES provides smoke control system design services for indoor parking lots, industrial facilities, technical volumes, tunnel-like structures and large closed areas. This service; It is not limited to just fan selection. A holistic system design is created by evaluating the architectural structure of the project, fire scenario, air flow directions, escape routes, exhaust points, fresh air need, automation scenarios and field conditions together.

Jet fan systems; They are modern mechanical ventilation solutions used to direct air flow in indoor parking lots, evacuate exhaust gases from vehicles and ensure controlled removal of smoke in case of fire. NOVVES analyzes these systems on a project-specific basis, determines the correct fan placement and supports the smoke control scenario with engineering data.

The main goal in smoke control system design is; To protect indoor air quality under normal working conditions, to limit the uncontrolled spread of smoke in case of fire, to support the safety of escape routes and to create an air flow organization that will facilitate the intervention of fire brigades.

approach.title: NOVVES Smoke Control Design Approach
approach.intro: Smoke control design for NOVVES is not just about equipment placement; It is an important part of the project's security strategy. The following elements are evaluated together in each project:
items: Fire scenario and possible smoke spread directions
Escape routes, ramps, shafts and critical access points
Jet fan, exhaust fan and fresh air fan placement
Location of CO, smoke and heat sensors
MCC / DDC control cabinet and automation scenarios
Regulation, standard and project specification requirements
approach.closing: Thanks to this approach, the system is evaluated not only according to theoretical calculations, but also according to real field conditions and air movement behavior at the time of fire.

items.title: Jet Fans
items.text: Jet fans are the main air direction elements of the system. Mounted on the ceiling, it creates high-speed airflow and directs polluted air or smoke towards exhaust points. Axial jet fan or radial jet fan types can be used depending on the project need. Axial jet fans can be selected according to one-way or two-way operating principle.

items.title: Exhaust Fans
items.text: Exhaust fans discharge polluted air, CO concentration or smoke generated in case of fire, directed by jet fans, to the outdoor environment in a controlled manner. In smoke evacuation scenarios, the temperature resistance, flow capacity and operating time of the fans are evaluated according to the project conditions.

items.title: Fresh Air Fans
items.text: Fresh air fans are used when natural openings are not sufficient or fresh air intake cannot be provided in the desired direction. These fans support the air balance of the system and contribute to the organization of pressure and air movement to help prevent smoke from being directed to escape routes.

items.title: sensors
items.text: CO sensors, smoke sensors, heat detection elements and related field equipment produce data for the automation infrastructure of the system. Information from the sensors is transmitted to the control panel in line with the determined limit values ​​and fire scenarios.

items.title: Automation and Control System
items.text: MCC / DDC control panels ensure that jet fans, exhaust fans, fresh air fans and sensors operate according to the scenario. System; It can be activated automatically according to different operating scenarios such as normal ventilation, CO evacuation and fire mode. It can be integrated with the building management system when necessary.

items.title: Reduces Channel Requirement
items.text: Since jet fan systems work by directing air, they offer a more flexible solution than traditional duct type ventilation systems. In this way, the need for wide duct lines and numerous grilles or diffusers can be reduced.

items.title: Saves Space
items.text: Ceiling height and usable volume are critical in indoor car parks. Thanks to their compact structure, jet fans take up less space and contribute to more efficient use of architectural space.

items.title: Supports Energy Efficiency
items.text: When working with CO sensors and automation system, jet fans can be activated only when needed. Energy consumption can be optimized thanks to variable speed control and scenario-based operation.

items.title: Controls Smoke and Heat Evacuation
items.text: In case of fire, the jet fan system helps reduce the uncontrolled spread of smoke and direct the smoke to designated exhaust points. This approach supports the safety of escape routes and contributes to a more controlled fire response.

items.title: Provides Ease of Maintenance and Operation
items.text: As the channel density decreases, cleaning, maintenance and access processes can be managed more easily. Fewer mechanical components simplify the organization of maintenance in the operating process.

items.title: Easily Adapts to Architectural Structure
items.text: Jet fan systems can be designed flexibly according to different car park geometries, ramp locations, column placements and ceiling heights. In this way, applicable solutions can be developed in new projects and existing structures.

items.title: Optimizes Initial Investment and Operating Costs
items.text: Correctly designed jet fan systems; It can optimize the initial investment cost by reducing the need for channels, grilles and diffusers. Automation-supported working scenarios contribute to the management of long-term energy and operating costs.

designFactors.title: Important Factors in Design
designFactors.intro: In order for the smoke control system to operate efficiently and safely, all architectural, mechanical, electrical and operational conditions must be evaluated together from the first stage of design.
paragraphs: Placement of axial fans, smoke and heat discharge fans, fresh air fans and jet fans in the jet fan project; It should be designed taking into account the noise level, the need for air direction, the absence of dead zones where fresh air cannot reach, ease of installation, maintenance access, safety of escape routes and smoke diversion strategy in case of fire.

In closed car parks, vehicle exhaust gases, CO concentration, user traffic, vehicle circulation, ramps, columns, shafts, door openings and natural ventilation facilities directly affect air movement. Therefore, correct positioning of jet fans is critical for the system to direct the air flow in the most efficient way.

In a fire scenario, the aim is to prevent the uncontrolled spread of smoke and promote the safest possible evacuation conditions. For this reason, the operating scenario of the fans, sensor locations, automation panel, fire detection system and building management system integration should be planned together.

In necessary projects, CFD analysis is used to evaluate air flow, smoke dispersion, jet fan effect, dead zones, exhaust points and evacuation scenarios numerically. CFD-supported design helps verify fan placement and analyze system performance on a project-by-project basis.

meta.title: Maintenance and Performance Control | novels
meta.description: NOVVES maintenance and performance control — safe, efficient and long-lasting operation of fans, motors and ventilation systems.

hero.subtitle: Technical maintenance service for long-lasting, safe and efficient operation in fan, motor and ventilation systems.

paragraphs: NOVVES provides maintenance and performance control services for fan systems, jet fans, smoke extraction fans, axial fans, industrial fans, air handling units, chiller-supported HVAC systems, control panels and automation infrastructures.

Regular maintenance and performance control are as critical as correct product selection and correct installation in ventilation systems. Over time, contamination, vibration, bearing wear, engine load increase, electrical connection problems, sensor errors, air flow decrease or automation scenario problems may negatively affect system efficiency.

NOVVES maintenance and performance control service; It ensures that mechanical, electrical, aerodynamic and operational controls are evaluated together to support the safe, efficient and sustainable operation of the system.

items.title: Fan and Motor Controls
items.desc: Fan body, propeller, motor, fasteners, bearings, vibration elements, protection cages and mechanical connections are checked. Basic operating values ​​such as motor operating current, motor direction, noise, vibration and heating are evaluated.

items.title: Jet Fan System Control
items.desc: In closed car park jet fan systems, fan placement, air direction performance, engine operation, connection points, vibration level, automation signals and scenario-based operating status are checked.

items.title: Smoke Evacuation Fan Control
items.desc: In smoke and heat extraction fans, engine, propeller, body, connection equipment, electrical infrastructure, control panel and operating conditions depending on the fire scenario are evaluated.

items.title: Air Handling Unit and HVAC Controls
items.desc: Air handling unit fans, filter status, motor-fan group, belt-pulley structure, dampers, sensors, automation connections, air flow rate and system operating conditions are checked.

items.title: Chiller Assisted System Control
items.desc: In chiller-assisted HVAC systems, performance impacts associated with fan-coil, air handling unit, automation and air-side equipment are evaluated holistically. Technical guidance to optimize system balance is presented in the form of a report.

items.title: Automation and Control Panel Control
items.desc: MCC / DDC panels, frequency inverters, contactors, protection equipment, sensor connections, fire alarm signals, CO sensors and BMS integration are checked.

items.title: Performance Measurement and Evaluation
items.desc: System operating values; It is evaluated in terms of air flow rate, pressure, motor current, vibration, sound level, temperature, fan speed and operating scenarios. Optimization suggestions are offered when necessary.

items.title: Preliminary Evaluation
items.desc: System type, product model, project information, working conditions, maintenance history and existing complaints are evaluated.

items.title: Field Control
items.desc: NOVVES technical team carries out mechanical, electrical and operational checks in the field. Fan, motor, panel, sensor, connection equipment and system components are examined.

items.title: Basic Performance Controls
items.desc: Air flow, motor operating current, fan speed, sound, vibration, heating, automation responses and system behavior are controlled.

items.title: Failure Risk and Nonconformity Detection
items.desc: Loose connections, vibration sources, engine strain, sensor errors, incorrect operating scenarios, maintenance deficiencies or performance losses are identified.

items.title: Optimization Suggestions
items.desc: Speed ​​adjustment, automation scenario, maintenance plan, spare parts need, cleaning or technical improvement suggestions are prepared for the system to operate more efficiently.

items.title: Reporting
items.desc: Checks made, detected nonconformities, suggestions and points requiring urgent intervention, if any, are recorded with a technical service form or maintenance report.

items.title: Periodic Maintenance Planning
items.desc: Periodic maintenance intervals can be planned according to the intensity of use of the system, working environment, product type and project criticality.

whyImportant.title: Why are Maintenance and Performance Control Necessary?

items.title: Reduces the Risk of Malfunction
items.text: Thanks to regular inspection, mechanical loosening, vibration, motor strain, electrical connection problems and sensor errors can be detected at an early stage.

items.title: Supports Energy Efficiency
items.text: Dirty, out-of-adjustment or stressed fan systems may consume more energy. Performance control contributes to more efficient operation of the system.

items.title: Extends System Life
items.text: Correct maintenance supports the healthier operation of fan, motor, bearing, propeller, panel and automation components.

items.title: Increases Business Security
items.text: Regular inspection of critical equipment such as smoke extraction fans, jet fans and indoor car park ventilation systems is of great importance for safe operation.

items.title: Prevents Performance Loss
items.text: Contamination, wear, incorrect adjustment or airflow problems that occur over time can reduce system performance. The maintenance and control process ensures early detection of these losses.

items.title: Strengthens the After-Sales Process
items.text: Regular maintenance records; It helps manage service, warranty, spare parts and technical support processes more accurately.

coordination.title: Holistic Technical Assessment
paragraphs: NOVVES maintenance and performance control service is not only equipment control; It is a technical service that evaluates the operating logic of the system, field conditions and engineering requirements together.

Our technical service team works in coordination with the NOVVES technical office when necessary and provides support on fan selection, automation scenario, spare parts, performance analysis and system optimization.
In this way, it is not just whether the system works or not; It is evaluated whether it works correctly, efficiently, safely and in accordance with the project purpose.

meta.title: Training and Technical Consultancy | novels
meta.description: NOVVES training and technical consultancy — engineering-oriented knowledge support for fans, smoke control, CFD, commissioning and automation.

hero.subtitle: Engineering-focused technical information support for product, system and project teams.

paragraphs: NOVVES provides training and technical consultancy services for fan systems, jet fans, smoke extraction fans, axial fans, industrial fans, air handling units, chiller-supported HVAC systems, automation panels and smoke control systems.

In ventilation and smoke control systems, as well as choosing the right product, understanding the system correctly, using it correctly, performing correct maintenance and interpreting it correctly by the project teams is also critical. NOVVES training and technical consultancy service; It provides information support to operating teams, maintenance personnel, project companies, mechanical installation teams, contractors, consultants and technical purchasing teams.

For NOVVES, training is not just about product description. Aim; It is to explain in an understandable way the operating principle of the system, safe usage rules, maintenance needs, automation scenarios, fan performance and project-specific technical requirements.

items.title: Fan Systems Training
items.desc: The working principles, usage areas, selection criteria and maintenance requirements of axial fans, jet fans, smoke extraction fans, industrial fans, roof fans and cell fans are explained.

items.title: Smoke Control Systems Training
items.desc: The working logic of smoke control systems in indoor car parks, industrial facilities and large volume structures, jet fan placement, exhaust and fresh air organization, fire scenarios and automation approach are explained.

items.title: CFD Analysis and Project Evaluation Consultancy
items.desc: Technical support is provided on how to read CFD analysis results and how to reflect air flow, smoke dispersion, temperature distribution, CO concentration, visibility and fan placement outputs into project decisions.

items.title: Commissioning and User Training
items.desc: After the system is put into operation, the operation or maintenance team is informed about basic usage, points that need attention, operating modes, alarm situations and maintenance periods.

items.title: Maintenance and Troubleshooting Training
items.desc: Common malfunctions in fan, motor, panel, sensor, automation and HVAC systems, basic control steps, maintenance needs and safe intervention limits are explained.

items.title: Automation and Control Scenarios Training
items.desc: Technical information is provided about MCC / DDC control panels, CO sensors, fire alarm signals, BMS integration, normal ventilation mode, fire mode and manual operation scenarios.

items.title: Product Selection and Technical Documentation Consultancy
items.desc: Evaluation is made together with the technical teams regarding fan selection, technical data sheets, product codes, performance values, certification scope, user manuals and project documents.

items.title: Needs Analysis
items.desc: The purpose of the training or consultancy request is determined. Participant profile, project type, product group, system scope and technical needs are evaluated.

items.title: Content Planning
items.desc: Training content; It is prepared according to product group, application area, project type, maintenance need, smoke control scenario or technical problem.

items.title: Technical Training / Consulting Session
items.desc: Education; It can be held on-site, online or in a project-specific technical meeting format. Explanation is made through products, system diagrams, application examples, maintenance steps and technical documents.

items.title: Q&A and Application Evaluation
items.desc: Participants' questions regarding the project, product, maintenance, malfunction, automation or commissioning processes are answered by the technical team.

items.title: Documentation and Tracking
items.desc: When necessary, training notes, technical documents, maintenance instructions, user manuals or project-specific suggestions are shared.

whyImportant.title: Why is Training and Technical Consultancy Necessary?

items.title: Ensures Correct Use of the System
items.text: Correct understanding of fan, jet fan, smoke extraction and automation systems; It reduces the risks of misuse, incorrect intervention and unnecessary malfunction.

items.title: Increases the Quality of Care
items.text: Maintenance teams' better knowledge of products and system components enables periodic checks to be carried out more accurately.

items.title: Shortens Fault Response Time
items.text: Knowing the basic fault symptoms, alarm conditions and control steps speeds up the initial evaluation process.

items.title: Strengthens Technical Decisions of Project Teams
items.text: Accurate information on fan selection, CFD analysis, smoke control design, automation scenario and technical documentation contributes to making healthier project decisions.

items.title: Supports Safe Business
items.text: Trained personnel in critical systems such as smoke extraction fans, jet fan systems and closed car park ventilation systems provide a significant advantage in terms of operational safety.

items.title: Supports Product Lifecycle and System Performance
items.text: Correct use and correct maintenance approach; It contributes to longer life and efficient operation of fan, motor, panel, sensor and system components.
